For a harness desk that already lives in Grok/xAI, the useful read is the shipping cadence plus the stack change, not another parameter-count meme. Watch for follow-on release notes once training actually lands.

body: Robotaxi Radar charted Tesla's Texas Robotaxi fleet jumping from 186 to 439 vehicles in a single month — roughly +136%. Anand retweeted the card overnight; for Austin readers that is the supply-side story after weekend wait-time complaints.
Fleet growth does not erase cabin UX or Cybercab scarcity, but it is the first hard count in a while that the network is expanding faster than a press-cycle anecdote.

body: Greg Isenberg's line is that the thin "GPT wrapper" era is giving way to domain-specific agent harnesses — the glue that owns tools, memory, evals, and product motion around a model. Anand retweeted it; X news also flags builders shifting that way.
If you already live in Cursor/Grok Bot land, this is the framing for why harness quality beats raw model shopping this week.

stories.headline: Fable 5.1 solves the Cyphral Distich, a 370-year-old cipher
stories.why_read: HN ~1007 — Claude Fable recovers Urquhart's royalist plaintext in under an hour.
body: Vals.ai reports Claude Fable 5.1 solved Sir Thomas Urquhart's Cyphral Distich — a 64-number cryptogram unsolved since the 1650s and still listed among famous open ciphers. After ~44 minutes and 176k tokens with no human interjections, it keyed each number to Urquhart's matching Proquiritation and recovered the royalist prayer for Charles II.

The write-up also claims a near-complete solve of the larger Cyphral Octastich. HN piled on (~1007 pts): persistence on archival puzzles, not flashy cryptanalysis, is the takeaway — and a reminder that attention bottlenecks are moving.

stories.headline: HP ZGX Fury orderable: GB300 Superchip, 748GB unified memory
stories.why_read: StorageReview + HN — deskside Grace Blackwell Ultra with a Red Hat AI Factory edge plan.
body: StorageReview reports HP's ZGX Fury AI station is now orderable: one NVIDIA GB300 Grace Blackwell Ultra Desktop Superchip, 748GB coherent unified memory, up to ~20 petaFLOPS FP4, ConnectX-8 400GbE, and tower-or-5U packaging. HP is pitching it as shared departmental inference, not a personal GPU toy, with Ubuntu 24.04, Z Runtime, and Red Hat AI Factory collaboration planned for the edge.
Pricing was not disclosed. For local-AI and systems readers, this is the DGX-Station-class deskside race filling in beside MSI's WS300.
